promptText: When an owner wants a collection or soft-brand option for a hotel conversion in Mexico, which brands are commonly considered?
rawResponse:
Here are the most commonly considered soft-brand or collection options that hotel owners often explore when converting existing properties in Mexico. These brands allow for affiliation with global operators while preserving a property's unique identity—especially relevant in markets like Mexico with abundant independent hotels:

Major international chains offering soft-brand or collection options:

- Marriott International:
  - Autograph Collection
  - Tribute Portfolio
  - Design Hotels ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))
  - The Luxury Collection (one of the earliest soft brands, often used for historic-property conversions) ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriott_International?utm_source=openai))

- Hilton:
  - Curio Collection
  - Tapestry Collection ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))
  - Spark by Hilton (launched specifically as a conversion-friendly, midscale soft brand; introduced in Mexico in February 2025) ([thegatewithbriancohen.com](https://thegatewithbriancohen.com/what-is-a-conversion-brand-and-why-you-might-want-to-avoid-it/?utm_source=openai))

- IHG (InterContinental Hotels Group):
  - Vignette Collection ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))
  - Garner (a conversion-oriented brand targeting lower-end properties in Mexico, rolled out in 2023) ([thegatewithbriancohen.com](https://thegatewithbriancohen.com/what-is-a-conversion-brand-and-why-you-might-want-to-avoid-it/?utm_source=openai))

- Wyndham Hotels & Resorts:
  - Trademark Collection
  - Registry Collection
  - Dolce Hotels and Resorts ([development.wyndhamhotels.com](https://development.wyndhamhotels.com/convert-your-existing-hotel?utm_source=openai))

- Accor Group:
  - MGallery
  - Emblems Collection (positioned at luxury tier) ([hoteldevelopmentguide.com](https://hoteldevelopmentguide.com/hotel-brands/?utm_source=openai))

- Choice Hotels:
  - Ascend Hotel Collection (considered the first soft brand in the industry) ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))

- Hyatt:
  - Unbound Collection ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))

- Best Western:
  - BW Premier Collection ([insights.ehotelier.com](https://insights.ehotelier.com/insights/2025/02/26/case-study-in-soft-brand-success-with-faro-blanco-resort-autograph-collection/?utm_source=openai))

- Preferred Hotels & Resorts (although more of an independent consortium than a traditional soft brand, emphasizing independent and boutique hotels) ([hospitalitas.com.mx](https://hospitalitas.com.mx/2022/07/28/entendiendo-el-modelo-de-negocio-de-las-soft-brands-hoteleras/?utm_source=openai))

---

Summary Overview:

These soft or conversion-friendly brands offer a spectrum for owners in Mexico—from **upper-midscale curated collections** like Trademark (Wyndham) and Spark (Hilton), to **upper-upscale or luxury offerings** such as Autograph (Marriott), Curio (Hilton), MGallery (Accor), and The Luxury Collection (Marriott). IHG’s Vignette and Garner cater to different market tiers and conversion needs. Choice’s Ascend is well suited for boutique-style properties that want flexibility in identity, while Preferred caters to independent-luxe conversions outside of rigid branding constraints.

If you need help narrowing down further—for example, by positioning tier (midscale vs. luxury), target guest profile, operational flexibility, loyalty program access, or franchise versus management agreement models—I’d be happy to assist.
